text_blocks.snippet: Depression carries significant risks, including impacts on physical and mental health, relationships, and overall quality of life. Untreated depression can lead to chronic diseases, substance abuse, suicidal thoughts, and even death.
snippet_highlighted_words: impacts on physical and mental health, relationships, and overall quality of life

list.title: Increased risk of chronic diseases:
list.snippet: Depression can elevate the risk of developing conditions like heart disease, diabetes, and stroke.

list.title: Pain and physical illness:
list.snippet: Depression can cause or worsen physical pain and contribute to other medical conditions.

list.title: Substance abuse:
list.snippet: Individuals with depression may turn to alcohol or drugs to cope with their symptoms, leading to substance use disorders.

list.title: Relationship problems:
list.snippet: Depression can strain relationships with family and friends, leading to conflicts and social isolation.

list.title: Poor academic or work performance:
list.snippet: Depression can make it difficult to concentrate, leading to academic or work-related issues.

list.title: Suicidal thoughts and behavior:
list.snippet: Depression is a major risk factor for suicidal ideation and attempts.

list.title: Self-harm:
list.snippet: Some individuals with depression may engage in self-harming behaviors, such as cutting.

list.title: Lower quality of life:
list.snippet: Depression can significantly reduce overall quality of life, impacting daily functioning and well-being.

list.title: Family history:
list.snippet: Having a family history of depression increases the risk.

list.title: Stressful life events:
list.snippet: Major life changes, such as the loss of a loved one or a job, can trigger depression.

list.title: Personality traits:
list.snippet: Certain personality traits, like low self-esteem or perfectionism, can make individuals more vulnerable to depression.

list.title: Gender:
list.snippet: Women are more likely to experience depression than men, potentially due to hormonal factors and societal pressures.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Depression can affect people of all ages, but older adults may be more susceptible due to factors like social isolation and chronic illness.

list.title: Chronic illness:
list.snippet: Individuals with chronic illnesses like diabetes or chronic pain may be at higher risk.

list.title: Substance abuse:
list.snippet: Substance abuse can both contribute to and be a consequence of depression.

list.title: Other mental health conditions:
list.snippet: Conditions like anxiety or eating disorders can increase the risk of depression.

list.title: Lack of social support:
list.snippet: Social isolation and lack of social support can increase vulnerability to depression.

text_blocks.snippet: While not all cases of depression can be prevented, certain measures can help reduce the risk. These include maintaining a healthy lifestyle (including regular exercise and a balanced diet), managing stress, seeking social support, and addressing any underlying mental health conditions.

Early diagnosis and treatment of depression are crucial to minimize its negative consequences. Treatment options include therapy (such as cognitive behavioral therapy or interpersonal therapy), medication (such as antidepressants), and lifestyle changes.
